## 1. Data integrity

- The latest row (2026-11-18) is O 510.07 / H 532.17 / L 495.20 / C 530.14 / V 33,277,645. It comes from the verified snapshot, which I treat as the source of truth.
- The indicator-tool values at 2026-11-18 match the snapshot to rounding, so I found no discrepancies. This covers the 10 EMA, 50 SMA, 200 SMA, RSI, Bollinger middle, MACD and ATR.
- The Bollinger upper and lower bands (602.84 and 426.43), the MACD signal (-12.49) and the histogram (+4.45) come only from the snapshot. I did not pull them separately.
- VWMA (501.48) comes only from the indicator tool. The snapshot does not list it, so it can't be cross-checked.
- I can't confirm whether the 2026-11-18 volume is a final end-of-day figure. Treat the comparison of today's volume with prior days with some caution.

## 2. Indicators chosen and why

I picked eight complementary indicators and avoided redundant ones:

| Role | Indicator |
|---|---|
| Short-term trend | 10 EMA |
| Medium-term trend | 50 SMA |
| Long-term trend | 200 SMA |
| Momentum | MACD (with its signal and histogram from the snapshot) |
| Overbought/oversold | RSI |
| Volatility and range | Bollinger middle (with upper and lower bands) |
| Volatility for risk sizing | ATR |
| Volume-weighted trend | VWMA |

## 3. Price narrative (from the OHLCV data)

- **Rally into early June:** the close rose from 420.99 (05-18) to 542.52 (06-03).
- **Choppy mid-year range:** closes ran roughly 430–580 from June to early August. The low close was 429.56 (07-29). The high was 580.91 (06-30).
- **Quiet late summer:** price drifted at 456–480 in late August and early September, with volume mostly 12–20M.
- **September breakout:** the close went from 559.82 (09-18) to 615.52 (09-21) on 44.5M shares, the heaviest volume of that stretch. Price then held roughly 600–650 into early October. The highest close in the window is 649.42 (10-06).
- **October–November drawdown:**
  - The close fell to 528.75 (10-16) and 507.93 (10-22).
  - It bounced to 578.44 (10-28).
  - It then dropped from 566.42 (10-29) to 504.80 (10-30), about -10.9% on 39.7M shares.
  - The capitulation low was a close of 404.40 on 11-05 (intraday low 402.10) on 71.2M shares. That is the heaviest volume in the whole window and about -17% on the day.
- **V-shaped rebound:** the close went 449.04 (11-06) → 508.58 (11-09) → 585.30 (11-12), about +45% from the 404.40 low. Volume stayed at 45–55M.
- **Pullback and bounce:** the close fell to 534.06 (11-13, about -8.8%), then 504.28 (11-16) and 503.41 (11-17). Today's close of 530.14 is about +5.3% on the day. The candle has a long lower wick (low 495.20) and closed in the upper part of its range.

## 4. Indicator readings

**Trend structure (moving averages)**
- The close of 530.14 is above the 10 EMA (519.17), which gives a short-term bullish tilt.
- It is below the 50 SMA (555.22) by about 25 points. The 50 SMA has risen gently, from 538.23 on 10-19 to 555.22, so it is a lagging overhead reference.
- It is well above the 200 SMA (427.18), and the 200 SMA is still rising, from 395.87 on 10-19. The 50 SMA sits above the 200 SMA, so the long-term structure is still constructive. I can't date when that crossover occurred from this data.
- The 10 EMA has fallen from 576.62 (10-19) to a low of 487.93 (11-06). It then recovered to about 519–523 and is flat to slightly up. Price is back above it for the first time since the 11-13 pullback began.
- The 10 EMA and 50 SMA were about 36 points apart on 11-18 (519.17 vs 555.22). Medium-term trend is in a repair phase, not a confirmed uptrend.

**Momentum (MACD and RSI)**
- MACD is -8.03 against a signal of -12.49, so the histogram is +4.45. MACD is above its signal, which is a bullish crossover, but both are still below zero.
- MACD has recovered from -30.20 (11-06), but it is still negative. It crossed below zero between 10-19 (+3.28) and 10-20 (-0.59). So this is a momentum recovery inside a medium-term momentum deficit, not a regained uptrend.
- RSI is 50.34, which is neutral. It hit a low of 29.75 on 11-05, the only oversold reading in the window, coinciding with the 404.40 close. It peaked at 57.48 on 11-12 and never approached 70.
- The RSI path (oversold, then neutral) fits a relief rally that has not yet turned into trend strength. I'm not claiming divergence.

**Volatility (Bollinger and ATR)**
- The Bollinger middle (20 SMA) is 514.64, with the upper band at 602.84 and the lower at 426.43. Price is just above the middle, in the central part of a very wide band.
- The band is about 176 points wide, roughly 34% of the middle. The middle has fallen steadily from 606.53 (10-19) and is flattening (519.02 on 11-13 → 514.64).
- ATR is 40.33, up from about 26.0 on 10-29, a rise of roughly 55%. That is about 7.6% of the current price. The post-earnings-style swings (10-30 to 11-13) pushed volatility to a clearly higher regime.
- ATR has eased slightly from its 41.94 peak on 11-13, so volatility may be starting to cool, but it remains elevated.

**Volume-weighted view (VWMA)**
- VWMA is 501.48, below both the price (530.14) and the 10 EMA. It has fallen from 598.12 (10-19), then stabilised at about 501–506 over the last five sessions.
- Price above VWMA means the heavily traded recent prices (the 11-05 to 11-12 sessions) were below the current price. Buyers who stepped in on the heavy-volume rebound are in profit.
- The volume trend is fading: 55.4M (11-12) → 49.4M → 37.1M → 36.3M → 33.3M. The rebound is not yet being confirmed by fresh high volume.

## 5. Synthesis

**Bullish factors**
- Price is above the 10 EMA, the VWMA and the Bollinger middle.
- The MACD histogram is positive and RSI has recovered from oversold.
- The 200 SMA is still rising, and price is far above it.
- Today's candle shows buyers defended the area near 495.20.

**Bearish and cautionary factors**
- Price is below the falling-then-flat Bollinger middle trend and below the 50 SMA (555.22).
- MACD is still below zero.
- The 10 EMA is still below the 50 SMA.
- Volume has faded for four straight sessions.
- ATR is high, and the 11-12 to 11-13 reversal (585.30 → 534.06) shows how quickly rebounds have been sold.

**Overall read:** mixed to neutral. The market is in a high-volatility, post-selloff consolidation. Short-term momentum has turned up, but medium-term trend confirmation is not yet in place.

## 6. Reference levels and scenarios

These levels are drawn from the data above. I have not verified that any of them has acted as support or resistance historically.

| Reference | Value | Source |

| Upside: 50 SMA | 555.22 | Snapshot |
| Upside: recent swing close/high | 585.30 close, 594.00 high (11-12) | OHLCV |
| Upside: 10-28 close | 578.44 | OHLCV |
| Near-term pivots | 519.17 (10 EMA), 514.64 (Bollinger mid) | Snapshot |
| Downside: recent closes | 503.41 (11-17), 504.28 (11-16) | OHLCV |
| Downside: 11-17 intraday low | 480.50 | OHLCV |
| Downside: 11-05 close / intraday low | 404.40 / 402.10 | OHLCV |
| Long-term trend | 427.18 (200 SMA) | Snapshot |

**Constructive scenario:** price holds above the 10 EMA and Bollinger middle (about 515–519), MACD crosses above zero, and a close above the 50 SMA (555.22) comes with volume that rebuilds above the recent 33–37M level. That would point toward the 11-12 high area.

**Cautionary scenario:** a close back below roughly 514–519 would return price to the 11-16/11-17 closes near 503–504. Below that, the 11-17 low of 480.50 is the next reference. Loss of that level would put the 11-05 low zone back in play.

**Risk sizing:** ATR is 40.33, so a one-ATR move is about 7.6% of price. As arithmetic only, 2×ATR below the 530.14 close is about 449.5 and 1.5×ATR below is about 469.6. Because daily ranges are this wide, position size should be reduced, or stops widened, relative to calmer periods.

- **Nvidia in the headlines:** Barron's ("Stocks That Explain Today's Market") and the WSJ ("Stocks to Watch") both led with Nvidia during the week. Check Nvidia's reported results and guidance directly, since they set sentiment for AI accelerator names.
- **Nvidia market-cap market:** Polymarket gives only a 6% chance that Nvidia is the world's largest company by market cap on Dec 31, down 7pp over the week. This is a thin read on AI-leadership sentiment, not an AMD signal.
- **Jensen Huang markets:** The Polymarket "AMD" search returned only Jensen Huang career-speculation markets with tiny volume (under $20k). They are not informative for AMD.

These are crowd-priced odds, not forecasts, and I can't corroborate them against FRED.

- **Anthropic:** The market on "Anthropic market cap below $1.25T on IPO day" jumped 18.6pp to 39%. It is a sentiment indicator for AI valuations, with unclear relevance to AMD.

**Reading for AMD:** The market is pricing low recession risk, low AI-bubble risk, and a hawkish Fed. That combination is supportive of AI-linked earnings but a headwind for high-multiple semiconductors if yields rise. AMD is a long-duration, high-multiple growth name, so a 25bp hike on 12-09 matters mainly through its effect on yields and the discount rate.

## 3. Broader market tone (headlines only)

- Take-Two (TTWO) surged on strong reviews of Grand Theft Auto VI (a Metacritic 99). Wells Fargo projects 65M copies by March. This is a consumer and gaming story, with only a loose link to AMD's gaming and console business.
- Motley Fool headlines mention a "stock market correction," but I don't know how deep or recent it is.
- Barron's reports that AI risks lifted cybersecurity stocks while software tries to "shrug off a slump."
- The Hewlett Packard Enterprise item ("What Has The Market Missed In HPE's Drop?") hints at weakness in some AI and server hardware names. I have no detail.
- HR Dive asks whether more companies will end H-1B programs. This is a minor tech-labor and policy item.

1. **Fill the gaps first.** Pull AMD price action, volume, and any news directly, and check Nvidia's latest earnings and guidance. Also check the actual fed funds rate, the 10-year yield, the latest CPI and unemployment readings, and the VIX. Trade decisions shouldn't rest on this report alone.

3. **Supermicro as a possible tailwind.** Look for primary-source confirmation, such as a press release, 8-K, or Supermicro commentary.
4. **Event risk.** The 12-09 FOMC and any Nvidia read-through are the nearest scheduled catalysts I can identify.
5. **Conviction is low.** The AMD-specific evidence is one unread headline. I'd treat this as macro context only and not as a trade signal.

# AMD (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.), Fundamental Report as of 2026-11-18

Sector: Technology / Semiconductors, NMS. Sources: `get_fundamentals`, quarterly balance sheet, cash flow and income statement (SEC EDGAR basis), and insider transactions. I had no news or filing-date tool, so I can't confirm exactly what was filed in the past week. The latest quarter in the statements is the period ended 2026-09-26 (fiscal Q3 2026).

## 1. Snapshot and valuation

- **Market cap:** about $877B. Price is roughly $500–530: $530 is implied by P/E × EPS, and the most recent insider sale was at about $503–508 on Nov 16.
- **52-week range:** $188.22 to $658.52. The 50-day average is $555 and the 200-day average is $426. The price is below the 50-day average and roughly 19% below the 52-week high, but still well above the 200-day average.
- **Beta:** 2.54, so expect large swings.
- **Trailing multiples:**
  - P/E (TTM) is 113x on TTM EPS of $4.68.
  - Price/book is 12.7x, with book value of $41.70 per share.
  - Price/sales is about 19x on TTM revenue of $45.4B.
  - EV/EBITDA is about 79x. This is my calculation: EV of roughly $879B, using market cap plus about $9.2B of implied debt minus $7.4B of cash, over TTM EBITDA of $11.14B.
- **Forward multiples:** Forward P/E is 30.1x and PEG is 0.45, based on forward EPS of $17.64. That is about 3.8x TTM EPS. The latest quarterly GAAP EPS of $1.46 annualizes to only about $5.84. The forward multiple therefore depends entirely on a very steep analyst earnings ramp that I could not verify. The estimates are probably non-GAAP and/or for a later fiscal year.
- **Free cash flow:** TTM FCF is $7.36B, a yield of about 0.84% on market cap.
- **Dividend:** none.

## 2. Income statement trend

Revenue, gross profit, operating income and net income are in $M. The Q4 2025 column is absent from the vendor data.

| Q1'26 (Mar-26) | 10,253 | 5,416 (52.8%) | 1,476 (14.4%) | 1,383 | 0.84 |
| Q2'26 (Jun-26) | 11,536 | 6,203 (53.8%) | 1,990 (17.3%) | 2,297 | 1.38 |
| **Q3'26 (Sep-26)** | **13,377** | **7,210 (53.9%)** | **2,832 (21.2%)** | **2,428** | **1.46** |

- **Growth:** Q3'26 revenue grew +44.7% year on year and +16.0% quarter on quarter. Q2'26 grew about +50% year on year and Q1'26 about +38%. Revenue is about 2.5x the Q1'23 level of $5.35B.
- **Operating leverage:** Implied operating expenses (gross profit minus operating income) were about $4.38B in Q3'26, up about 25% year on year against revenue up about 45%. The incremental operating margin year on year was about 38%.
- **Share count:** Implied diluted shares are about 1.66B, flat year on year. Growth has not been driven by buybacks.
- **Comparison quirk:** Q2'25 operating income was –$134M and gross margin 39.8%, a depressed base that flatters some year-on-year comparisons.
- **Data discrepancy:** The fundamentals "Gross Profit" of $25.44B implies a TTM gross margin of 56%. That is above every reported quarterly GAAP margin shown, so it is likely on a different basis. Rely on the statement figures.
- **Margins in the fundamentals feed:** Profit margin is 16.8%, operating margin 17.8%, ROE 12.0% and ROA 5.9%.

## 3. Balance sheet

All figures are at 2026-09-26, in $M.

| Total assets | 94,812 | 84,464 | 79,642 | 76,926 |

- **Liquidity and leverage:** The current ratio is 2.73x (39,471 / 14,486, which matches the fundamentals feed). Debt/equity is 0.13x, implying about $9.2B of debt.
- **Implied liabilities:** Total liabilities are not tagged by the filer. Assets minus equity gives about $26.4B, up from about $17.2B a quarter earlier. That is a roughly $9.2B jump, of which only about $2.4B is current liabilities. The remaining roughly $6.8B rise in non-current liabilities is not explained by the tool output. Financing inflow in the quarter was about $2.3B, so this needs a look at the 10-Q footnotes (debt, supply or customer commitments).
- **Asset base:** The jump from $12.4B (Dec 2021) to $66.9B (Mar 2022) reflects the Xilinx acquisition. Most of the asset base is acquisition-related, which is why ROE is only about 12%.

## 4. Cash flow

The vendor reports cash flow year to date, so I differenced it to get quarterly figures. Figures are in $M.

## 1. The business is accelerating

Fiscal Q3'26 (September quarter) revenue was **$13.38B, up 44.7% year on year and 16% sequentially**. The path was $10.25B (Q1) → $11.54B (Q2) → $13.38B (Q3). Profit is growing faster than revenue:

- **Gross margin:** 53.9%, a four-quarter high.

- **Operating expenses:** up about 25% against revenue up about 45%. That is about a 38% incremental operating margin, which is what scalable growth looks like.

## 2. The balance sheet can fund the build-out

- Debt/equity is 0.13x and equity is $68.4B.
- There is no dividend, so every dollar goes back into the growth ramp.
